title: Echo Flight incident
place_text: Echo Flight, Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana

tellings.difference: Told by the host, who places it eight days before Salas's own incident and ties it to later Malmstrom cases.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about the 1967 Echo Flight missile shutdown at Malmstrom.

plain: In 1967, at Echo Flight, a group of ten nuclear missiles at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, all ten missiles are said to have suddenly shut down while guards reported something strange overhead. A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas relays the account of the officer in charge, Walt Feele, who at first "couldn't believe what they were saying," before "all 10 of his missiles went down." Michels places it eight days before Salas's own similar incident and links it to later cases at Malmstrom. If true, it would mean something could switch off American nuclear weapons.
